primary_sources.title: Mazur and Mottola, Weyl Cohomology and the Effective Action for Conformal Anomalies
primary_sources.reviewed: Section IV, equations (38)-(46), conformal Ricci transformation, Paneitz operator and local trace variation.
primary_sources.use: Independent curvature/anomaly convention and exact independence of the canonical conformal derivative. Their discarded surface terms do not replace the retained boundary action.

source_access: Primary section and formulas opened directly; no downloaded-byte digest claimed.
strongest_comparator: The preceding mixed-boundary result leaves the shape-dependent nonlinear trace forcing and pure shape cutoff action open. The earlier pointwise-forcing tail argument does not apply to arbitrary H2 shape profiles.
hardest_step: Write the entire quadratic trace as F0-D F1+D^2 F2 before taking weak limits, and transfer L1+L2 forcing through the third-order tail equation including the delta contact in the Green derivative.
new_consequence: The full energy-class first-order shape leaves the persistent second-order trace/action combination unchanged within the stated expansion. The pure shape quadratic cutoff coefficient must supply the opposite explicit oscillatory vector if the total quadratic action is to converge.
remaining_quantum_gap: The limiting geodesic-seam form estimates do not by themselves control the canonical second variation on moving finite-cut domains. The pure shape cutoff limit remains unproved.
regulator_contract: Original fixed background cuts, paired domain and subtraction. Weak/logarithmic limits are necessary diagnostics; no physical averaging prescription or new counterterm.
verification_scope: Full coupled symbolic action/curvature agreement, charged unexpanded trace Taylor fixtures, H2 concentration tests and explicit Green convolution with contact. No canonical determinant, actual nonlocal shape solution or physical benchmark is evaluated.
